payload.text: Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a major aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. An independent teardown audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, retracting the earlier claim. The cell has a gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg, while projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. Its operating-temperature floor is 4 °C, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
